title_en: Zhenjiang Tanglao Yizhengzhai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Jilin Yizheng Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., Yizheng Group Jilin Province Medical Science and Technology Industrial Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy — dispute over unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: When reviewing a claim by a time-honored enterprise with certain popularity that, based on the right to the unique name of a well-known commodity and the right to an enterprise name as stipulated in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, seeks to prohibit a competitor from using its registered trademark and enterprise name, it is necessary to comprehensively consider factors such as the historical evolution of the time-honored enterprise and the scope of its existing social influence, the scope of popularity of the competitor and its commodities, and whether the competitor has the subjective intent to free-ride on the existing goodwill of the time-honored enterprise, in accordance with the legislative purpose, legal provisions, and judicial interpretations of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Even if the court, based on the above considerations, determines that the competitor does not constitute unfair competition, in order to better protect the time-honored enterprise while promoting the further development of the legitimate rights and interests of the competitor, the court may also require both parties to operate honestly and use their commodity names and trademarks in a standardized manner respectively, so as to prevent confusion and conflict among market entities, protect consumer rights, and maintain a fair competition order in the market.

full_text_en:
**Zhenjiang Tanglao Yizhengzhai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Jilin Yizheng Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., Yizheng Group Jilin Province Pharmaceutical Technology Industry Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy — dispute over unfair competition**

**[Ruling Summary]**

When examining whether a time-honored enterprise with a certain degree of notoriety may, based on the right to a unique name of a well-known commodity and the right to an enterprise name as provided under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, claim to prohibit a competitor in the same trade from using its registered trademark and enterprise name, it is necessary to comprehensively consider factors such as the historical evolution of the time-honored enterprise and the scope of its current social influence, the scope of the competitor's and its commodity's notoriety, and whether the competitor has the subjective intent to exploit the existing goodwill of the time-honored enterprise, in accordance with the legislative purpose, legal provisions, and judicial interpretations of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Even if the court, based on the above factors, determines that the competitor does not constitute unfair competition, in order to better protect the time-honored enterprise while also promoting the further development of the competitor's legitimate rights and interests, the court may also require both parties to operate honestly and use their commodity names and trademarks in a standardized manner, so as to prevent confusion and conflict between market entities, protect consumer rights and interests, and maintain a fair market competition order.

**Plaintiff:** Zhenjiang Tanglao Yizhengzhai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zhongshan East Road, Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province.

**Legal Representative:** Tang Zhenkai, Chairman of the Board of the company.

**Defendant:** Jilin Yizheng Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Yingxiong Street, Siping City, Jilin Province.

**Legal Representative:** Yu Chunjiang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

**Defendant:** Yizheng Group Jilin Province Pharmaceutical Technology Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Lishan Road, Siping City, Jilin Province.

**Legal Representative:** Yu Chunjiang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

**Defendant:** Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Dujiang South Road, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

**Legal Representative:** Zhang Qi, General Manager of the company.

**Defendant:** Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy, domiciled at: Jiefang Road, Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province.

**Person in Charge:** Yao Shengzhang, District Manager.

The plaintiff, Zhenjiang Tanglao Yizhengzhai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company), filed a lawsuit with the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province due to a dispute over unfair competition with the defendants Jilin Yizheng Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yizheng Group Company), Yizheng Group Jilin Province Pharmaceutical Technology Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yizheng Technology Company), Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" was founded in the early Kangxi period of the Qing Dynasty. Its refined "Yizheng Plaster" (formerly named Wanying Linggao, Yizheng Plaster) had miraculous curative effects and was well-known at home and abroad. A trademark featuring the "Portrait of Tang Elou" was registered as early as 1930. On November 27, 1992, Tang Zhenkai, a descendant of "Tanglao Yizhengzhai," established the plaintiff. In 1994, the "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" trademark was restored and registered, and the "Yizheng Plaster" was produced and sold. The "Portrait of Tang Elou" trademark is a well-known trademark of Zhenjiang City and a China Time-honored Brand. The plaster-making technique of Tanglao Yizhengzhai is an intangible cultural heritage at the provincial level of Jiangsu. The former site of "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" is a cultural relic protection unit in Zhenjiang City. Without the plaintiff's consent, the defendants Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company unilaterally used the characters "Yizheng" in their company names, mutually licensed each other to use the two Chinese characters "Yizheng" and similar trademarks, and used names containing the characters "Yizheng" on plasters. This caused confusion with the plaintiff's well-known commodity name "Yizheng Plaster," led to consumer misidentification, infringed upon the exclusive right to use the registered trademark, and constituted unfair competition. The defendants Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy sold the aforementioned infringing products, constituting joint infringement, and should bear joint and several civil liability according to law. Therefore, the court was requested to order: 1. Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company to immediately cease the unfair competition acts infringing upon the registered trademark right and publicly apologize in newspapers; 2. Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company to change their company names and be prohibited from using the characters "Yizheng" in their trade names; 3. Compensation for economic losses of RMB 10,000 (based on actual illegal profits); 4. Payment of reasonable expenses for stopping the infringement, including attorney fees of RMB 20,000, notarization fees of RMB 800, travel expenses of RMB 7,200, and typing and copying fees of RMB 400, totaling RMB 28,400; 5. Yizheng Group Company, Yizheng Technology Company, Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy to bear the litigation costs of this case.

**Defendants' Defense:** The two defendants argued that they had lawfully obtained the right to their enterprise names through registration with the local industrial and commercial authorities. Trademarks such as "Yizheng," "Yizhengxiao," and "Yizhengchun" were lawfully registered and approved for use. The "Yizheng" trademark (Registration No. 3743982), approved for use on plasters in Class 5, had been recognized as a Well-known Trademark of Siping City, a Famous Trademark of Jilin Province, and a China Well-known Trademark. Therefore, their use was lawful and did not constitute infringement. The plaintiff's "Portrait of Tang Elou" trademark and its "Yizheng" Chinese character trademark are not similar in terms of the shape, pronunciation, meaning, composition of the graphic, overall structure, three-dimensional shape, or color combination. The testimony of witnesses produced by the plaintiff at trial confirmed that the two products differ significantly in packaging, physical form, and appearance, and would not cause misidentification. The plaintiff is a member unit of the "China Time-honored Brand" association, not a "China Time-honored Brand" itself, and should not be entitled to special protection. In summary, the enterprise names, unique packaging, and trademarks of Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company did not infringe upon the plaintiff's lawful rights and did not constitute unfair competition. They requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

The defendants Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy did not submit a written statement of defense within the statutory defense period and did not appear in court to defend.

**Facts Found by the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court at First Instance:**

During the Kangxi period of the Qing Dynasty, Tang Shouyi, the ancestor of the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company's legal representative, established the "Tang Yizhengzhai" plaster shop, producing "Yizheng Plaster" (originally named, later changed) for treating injuries such as falls and fractures. The term "Yizheng" originated from the Tang family ancestral motto: "Wholeheartedly follow one virtue to cure and save people; correct others by first correcting oneself meticulously." In 1922, "Tang Yizhengzhai" was renamed "Tanglao Yizhengzhai." "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" and its product "Yizheng Plaster" have a long history. In the north, there was a tradition of giving "Yizheng Plaster" as dowry for daughters. Its influence once reached across the country and to Southeast Asia. Due to its significant influence, in order to prevent counterfeit products, the Qing government erected a stone tablet inscribed "Fengxian Leshi Yongjin" (Forever Prohibited by Imperial Decree) to ban counterfeiting of "Yizheng Plaster." This tablet is known as China's first anti-counterfeiting monument. In 1930, the ninth-generation descendant of Tang Shouyi registered the portrait of his father Tang Di (styled Elou) as a trademark for "Yizheng Plaster," which was a pioneering use of a portrait as a trademark in China. From the 1950s to the 1980s, production of "Yizheng Plaster" was interrupted, and it was renamed "Zhenjiang Plaster" for production and sale, achieving considerable market recognition. On November 27, 1992, Tang Zhenkai, a descendant of the Tang family, invested to establish the plaintiff company with a registered capital of USD 160,000, primarily producing and selling "Yizheng Plaster" brand plasters. On August 7, 1994, the company registered and was approved for a combined word and graphic trademark consisting of "Portrait of Tang Elou" and "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" (Trademark Registration Certificate No. 700302), approved for use on plasters in Class 5. Currently, due to historical reasons, the "Yizheng Plaster" produced by the plaintiff does not have a drug approval number and is mainly sold through in-clinic prescription and mail order, not entering pharmacies. In August 1996, the combined graphic and word trademark "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" plus "Portrait of Tang Elou" was awarded the title of First Zhenjiang Well-known Trademark. In June 2005, the plaintiff was rated as a member unit of the "China Time-honored Brand" by the China Time-honored Brand Working Committee under the China General Chamber of Commerce. In March 2007, the "Yizhengzhai" plaster-making technique was listed by the People's Government of Jiangsu Province as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Jiangsu Province.

The defendant Yizheng Group Company was established on April 23, 2003, with a registered capital of RMB 18.5 million, mainly producing tablets, plasters, granules, and other products. It has three subsidiaries: Jilin Yizheng Medical Technology Development Co., Ltd., the defendant Yizheng Technology Company, and Siping Chunjiang Medical Co., Ltd. Yizheng Technology Company was established on November 14, 2005, with a registered capital of RMB 8 million, mainly producing "Yizheng Tongxiao" plasters and other products. Yu Chunjiang is the legal representative of both Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company. Yizheng Group Company and its subsidiaries registered trademarks consisting of the Chinese characters or combined characters and graphics for "Yizheng," "Yizhengchun," and "Yizhengxiao," and mutually licensed their use. These trademarks are all currently valid. Among them, the "Yizheng" trademark (No. 3743982), approved for use on plasters in Class 5, was rated as a Famous Trademark of Jilin Province and a Well-known Trademark of Siping City on July 12, 2006, and May 15, 2007, respectively. On March 5, 2008, it was recognized as a China Well-known Trademark by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce. "Yizheng Tongxiao" plasters are mainly distributed through domestic pharmacies. The hygiene license number is "[2005] No. 004, Siwei Health Certification", and the approval document number is "[2006] No. 002, Jiwei Health Use". Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company primarily advertise their corporate image and products through company websites, CCTV, and some local satellite TV stations, and sell through pharmacies nationwide.

The defendants Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company argued that their use of the Chinese characters "Yizheng" as their enterprise name and registered trademark stems from their corporate motto: "Wholeheartedly do things; be upright and honorable."

The defendant Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy is a franchise store of the defendant Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. On August 9, 2007, the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company's agent ad litem purchased "Yizheng Tongxiao" plasters produced by the defendant Yizheng Technology Company at the Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy. Subsequently, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit based on trademark infringement and unfair competition, making the aforementioned claims.

During the court trial, after the court's clarification, the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company chose to pursue the case based on unfair competition, i.e., asserting that the defendants Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, without its consent, unilaterally used "Yizheng" as their enterprise name and product trademark name, which constituted unfair competition. It requested a judgment ordering them to cease use and pay damages.

**The disputed issues at first instance were:** Whether the conduct of the defendants Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company in using the Chinese characters "Yizheng" as their enterprise name and registering them as a trademark constituted unfair competition.

**The Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:**

The trade name in the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company's enterprise name is the five Chinese characters "Tanglao Yizhengzhai." After approval and registration, it has the prior right to use "Tanglao Yizhengzhai." The structure of this character combination is a modifier-head structure, with the core word being "Zhai" (Studio), and "Tanglao Yizheng" serving as modifiers indicating attribution and origin. Therefore, the two characters "Yizheng" alone cannot fully express the meaning implied by "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" or the distinctiveness and uniqueness of its enterprise name and trade name. The plaintiff cannot obtain the exclusive right to the two characters "Yizheng" and exclude others from using them simply because it registered its enterprise name and used "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" first.

The plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that the current geographical scope of its "Yizheng Plaster" product coincides with that of the products involved of the defendants Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, resulting in overlapping sales areas. Furthermore, within these areas, there was no evidence that the plaintiff's product, due to its sales duration, sales volume, target customers, duration, extent, and geographical scope of any publicity, or its protection as a well-known product, had achieved a certain market reputation and become known to the relevant public, thus constituting a well-known commodity. Considering the sales channels of both products, it can be inferred that the plaintiff's product has a smaller geographical scope than that of Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company. Since it does not enter pharmacies, there was no condition for confusion or misidentification in pharmacy sales. The two witnesses produced by the plaintiff also confirmed that consumers would not confuse or misidentify the two types of plasters with ordinary attention. In the aforementioned geographical areas, absent evidence that the plaintiff's product constituted a well-known commodity, although the plaintiff used "Yizheng" on its goods, there was no statutory reason to exclude others from using "Yizheng" as their commodity name based on prior use. The evidence submitted by Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company could demonstrate that their use of "Yizheng" as their enterprise name and product name was not in bad faith, and there was no evidence showing that Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company had maliciously engaged in name registration or exploited the goodwill generated by the plaintiff's trade name or product name. Moreover, both companies had lawfully obtained the right to use their enterprise names through registration with the local industrial and commercial authorities. Therefore, the evidence was insufficient to establish that Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company had unilaterally used the unique name of the plaintiff's plaster or used a similar name, causing confusion with the plaintiff's plaster and leading to purchaser misidentification. Although the product of Yizheng Technology Company entered the Zhenjiang area for sale, objectively overlapping with the plaintiff's sales area, the existing evidence showed that consumers would not confuse the source of the two goods. Even if confusion or misidentification were possible, the plaintiff's remedy would be to request Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company to add product identifiers to distinguish the two products, rather than seeking an order to cease using the two characters "Yizheng." The plaintiff's title as a member unit of the "China Time-honored Brand" is not equivalent to being a "China Time-honored Brand" itself and does not entitle it to exceptional legal protection. Finally, the plaintiff had for a long time only sold through clinic prescriptions and mail order, and did not provide evidence of investing corresponding human, financial, and material resources in brand promotion and publicity, allowing the distinctiveness of "Yizheng" in its enterprise name and product name "Yizheng Plaster" to weaken. In contrast, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company invested considerable funds in publicity, gradually enhancing the distinctiveness of names such as "Yizheng," "Yizheng Pharmaceutical," and "Yizheng Group." Granting the plaintiff's request would contravene the principle of fairness.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1, Article 128, and Article 130 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 20, 2008:

**Judgment:**

The claims of the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 2,200 shall be borne by the plaintiff Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company.

Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Jiangsu Higher People's Court. **Main grounds:** As a product of a time-honored brand, whether "Yizheng Plaster" is a well-known commodity should not be determined solely by advertising and promotion investment. Over the years, "Yizheng Plaster" has gained a good reputation among consumers due to its genuine ingredients and significant efficacy. Its long history and renown at home and abroad satisfy the conditions for a well-known commodity. As the specific name of "Yizheng Plaster," "Yizheng" enjoys the right to the unique name of a well-known commodity. The appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, by unilaterally using "Yizheng" as a commodity name and enterprise name, are likely to cause the relevant public to confuse and misidentify the source and producer of the two goods, constituting unfair competition. The appellant requests the reversal of the first-instance judgment and a new judgment in its favor.

The appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company argued: The first-instance judgment was based on clear facts and applied the law correctly. They requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The appellees Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy did not appear in court and did not submit a defense.

The Jiangsu Higher People's Court, upon second instance hearing, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

**Additional facts found:**

1. In the 54th year of the Kangxi reign, Tang Shouyi named his shop "Yizhengzhai" (later changed). In the 1st year of the Yongzheng reign, it was renamed "Yizhengzhai." In 1956, "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" was merged into Zhenjiang Traditional Chinese Medicine Factory after undergoing public-private partnership.

2. The appellant Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company stated at second instance: Each "Yizheng Plaster" (one piece) costs RMB 240 and can be applied repeatedly. The appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company stated at second instance: One box of "Yizheng Tongxiao" patches costs RMB 18, contains 10 patches, and each patch can be used for 10 days.

3. On July 2, 2008, the appellant Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company applied to the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter TRAB) for cancellation of the "Yizheng," "Yizhengxiao," and "Yizhengchun" trademarks registered by the appellee Yizheng Group Company. The TRAB ruled to maintain all three trademarks. Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, dissatisfied with the TRAB's decisions maintaining the "Yizheng" and "Yizhengxiao" trademarks, filed administrative lawsuits with the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, which both upheld the TRAB's decisions. Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company appealed to the Beijing Higher People's Court, which dismissed the appeal and affirmed the first-instance judgments.

**The disputed issues at second instance were:** 1. Whether the conduct of the appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company constituted unfair competition; 2. If the conduct of the appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company constituted unfair competition, what civil liability should they bear.

**The Jiangsu Higher People's Court held at second instance:**

1. The conduct of the appellees Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company in registering and using the "Yizheng" trademark does not constitute unfair competition.

Since the establishment of "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" during the Kangxi period of the Qing Dynasty, "Yizheng Plaster" was sold domestically and internationally due to its significant efficacy. The Qing government even erected a stone tablet "Fengxian Leshi Yongjin" to ban counterfeiting of "Yizheng Plaster." To this day, the appellant Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company and its "Yizheng Plaster" still enjoy a certain degree of recognition among relevant consumers: The "Tang Elou" trademark on "Yizheng Plaster" was awarded the title of First Zhenjiang Well-known Trademark; the "Tanglao Yizhengzhai Plaster-making Technique" was rated by the Jiangsu Provincial People's Government as one of the first batches of Jiangsu Provincial Intangible Cultural Heritage; Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company was also rated as a member unit of the "China Time-honored Brand" and received the honor of "China Reform and Opening-up Thirty Years China Time-honored Brand Inheritance and Innovation Outstanding Enterprise." Therefore, the historical goodwill and certain notoriety enjoyed by "Yizheng Plaster" should be affirmed and granted a degree of protection.

In this case, the appellant, Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, sought protection on the ground that it enjoyed the right to the unique name of a well-known commodity under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law for "Yizheng". For time-honored brand commodities, whether they can obtain protection as well-known commodities under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and relevant judicial interpretations should be comprehensively considered in light of factors such as the historical goodwill of the time-honored brand, rather than merely considering factors such as advertising and promotion expenditures. However, as far as this case is concerned, whether the appellant can, on this ground, claim to prohibit the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, from registering and using their well-known trademark "Yizheng" requires a comprehensive assessment based on the facts found in this case, combined with the legislative purpose of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, its provisions, and judicial interpretations. The court is of the opinion that the degree of recognition of "Yizheng Plaster" as determined by the existing evidence currently provided by Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company is insufficient to support its claim to use the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to prohibit Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company from registering and using their well-known trademark "Yizheng".

First, the historical goodwill of "Yizheng Plaster" was interrupted for many years due to factors such as its production under a changed name. The predecessor of the appellant, Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, was established during the Kangxi reign of the Qing Dynasty, and its "Yizheng Plaster" was sold both domestically and internationally due to its significant therapeutic effects. However, relevant historical documents also record that in the 1950s, after "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" underwent joint state-private management and was merged into Zhenjiang Traditional Chinese Medicine Factory, "Yizheng Plaster," with a reduced formula, was renamed "Zhenjiang Plaster Patch." It was not until 1992 that the descendants of the Tang family revived their ancestral business and re-established Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company. Therefore, because the appellant's predecessor had been transformed into a different entity, and the original authentic "Yizheng Plaster" had also ceased production and was renamed "Zhenjiang Plaster Patch," the historical goodwill accumulated since the Qing Dynasty for "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" and "Yizheng Plaster" had been interrupted for nearly forty years. As a result, the population aware of the historical goodwill of "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" and "Yizheng Plaster" is primarily composed of members of the relevant public in areas such as Zhenjiang, Jiangsu, who have knowledge of certain history.

Second, the expansion of "Yizheng Plaster"'s current social influence is limited due to the particularities of its production and sales model. Due to various factors such as financial constraints, the "Yizheng Plaster" currently produced by the appellant has not obtained a drug approval number. Consequently, this product still cannot be sold in pharmacies and can only be marketed through limited sales models such as in-clinic consultations and mail-order sales. This special sales channel results in a relatively limited scope of people aware of the "Yizheng Plaster" product. At the same time, because "Yizheng Plaster" has strict requirements regarding the selection of raw medicinal materials and production processes, it is currently unable to be produced on a large scale, and its production volume is limited. This also, to a certain extent, affects the external sales scale and sales volume of "Yizheng Plaster." All these factors make the current social influence of "Yizheng Plaster" relatively limited. Although the appellant has received honors such as "Member Unit of China Time-honored Brand" and introductions of "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" and "Yizheng Plaster" in relevant books indicate their long history, when determining whether "Yizheng Plaster" can obtain protection under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law in this case, the length of its historical inheritance is only one of the factors to be considered.

Third, the act of Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company in registering and using the "Yizheng" trademark does not violate legal provisions or commercial ethics, nor does it affect the maintenance of a proper competitive order. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law is a law that establishes and maintains orderly and fair competition. Its legislative purpose is to prevent confusion regarding the origin of goods, prohibit malicious free-riding, and, on that basis, maintain commercial ethics and a proper competitive order. In this case, the "Yizheng" trademark registered and used by Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company on ointment-type goods has, after many years of widespread use, become well-known to the relevant public, enjoys a high reputation, and was recognized as a well-known trademark in 2008, possessing relatively high recognition in the national market. The appellant has not provided evidence to prove that Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, when registering and using the "Yizheng" trademark, were free-riding on its existing goodwill. Furthermore, although products like "Yizheng Tongxiao" produced by Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company and "Yizheng Plaster" are both applicable to ailments such as muscle and bone pain, products like the "Yizheng Tongxiao" plaster, having an approval number, are mainly sold through pharmacies. Each piece of "Yizheng Tongxiao" costs RMB 1.8, has a usage time of approximately 24 hours, and cannot be reused. In contrast, "Yizheng Plaster" cannot yet be sold in pharmacies; each piece costs RMB 240, can be reused, and the appearance of the two types of products also differs. Therefore, due to the completely different appearance, usage methods, sales prices, and sales channels of products like "Yizheng Tongxiao" plaster compared to "Yizheng Plaster," the specific group of people aware of "Yizheng Plaster" is able to distinguish between the two without causing confusion or mistaken identification. Consequently, the act of Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company in registering and using the "Yizheng" trademark did not free-ride on the appellant's existing goodwill, does not cause confusion as to the source of the goods, does not violate legal provisions or commercial ethics, and does not affect the maintenance of a proper competitive order.

II. The use of "Yizheng" as their enterprise name by the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, does not constitute an act of unfair competition.

In this case, the appellant, Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, seeks protection on the ground of its right to an enterprise name under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Both the appellant and the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, obtained the right to their enterprise names after registration approved by the local industry and commerce authorities. When a conflict of rights arises between the parties concerning the use of enterprise names, whether the appellant can, on the ground of enjoying the right to an enterprise name as stipulated in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, claim to prohibit Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company from using the "Yizheng" character component in their names also requires a comprehensive assessment based on the facts found in this case, combined with the legislative purpose of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, its provisions, and judicial interpretations.

First, according to the relevant provisions of China's enterprise name registration administration, an enterprise name generally consists of an administrative division, a character component (字号), an industry, and an organizational form, with the character component being the core element. The character component in the enterprise name of the appellant, Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company, should be "Tanglao Yizhengzhai." Therefore, strictly speaking, it is not the same as the character component "Yizheng" of the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company. Second, even if "Yizheng" could be considered the core part of the appellant's character component, the appellant's current degree of recognition is still insufficient to support its use of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to prohibit Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company from lawfully using their "Yizheng" character component. Third, the appellant has not provided evidence to prove that Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, when registering the "Yizheng" character component, were free-riding on its existing goodwill or causing market confusion. Based on the above considerations, the court is of the opinion that determining the use of the "Yizheng" character component by Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company constitutes unfair competition against the appellant would result in expanded protection for the appellant's character component, which would be unfair to Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, who are lawfully using their character component.

In summary, the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, do not constitute unfair competition. The appellees, Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Dadesheng Pharmacy Chain Co., Ltd., Zhenjiang New Concept Pharmacy, legally sold products such as "Yizheng Tongxiao" plaster and thus also do not constitute infringement.

It must also be pointed out that the profound regional cultural characteristics and distinctive Chinese cultural traditions carried and embodied by "Yizheng Plaster" and "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" should still be encouraged and promoted, even in the modern market economy environment. Therefore, adhering to the principle of "respecting history while taking into account reality," and given that products like the "Yizheng Tongxiao" plaster produced by the appellees, Yizheng Group Company and Yizheng Technology Company, have already been sold in the Zhenjiang area, in order to better protect the intangible assets of the "Tanglao Yizhengzhai" time-honored brand, inherit its unique products and craftsmanship, carry forward the excellent cultural traditions it embodies, and also promote the further development of the "Yizheng" well-known trademark while preventing confusion and conflict among market players, both parties should each operate honestly, standardize the use of their respective product names and trademarks, and, when necessary, add distinguishing labels to protect consumer rights and maintain the normal competitive order of the market.

Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby renders the following judgment on May 25, 2011:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 760 shall be borne by Tanglao Yizhengzhai Company.

This judgment is final.
